svg.title: Copper Scroll entry 52: the rock opposite Zadok
svg.text: Schematic plan, north up. One arrangement the text allows; not a reconstruction of any real site.
Project reading: the seat at the top of the west-facing rock
The rock's face looks west, toward the garden of Zadok. No distance, size or depth is given.
The deposit lies under the great slab at the seat's base (one reading of “its base”).
the text's anchor; garden or court is
top of the rock · ראש הסלע (dashed)
SECTION west–east · schematic, not to scale
seat(?) cut in the top, the great slab
at its base, the gold (×) under the slab
Milik 1962: across the torrent from Zadok's tomb
The anchor is a tomb, with a torrent bed between.
Høgenhaven: the hoard on a rock opposite the monument.
Alternative reading · basis of the Kidron placement
The first word: what is at the top of the rock?
Project text: “seat(?)”. The letters shown, הכסה, match
none of the editors' readings; the lexicon rates it low.
Changes the feature, not the layout
Milik: “in its water channel”. Lefkovits: a spiral staircase,
and a sum of 10, 11 or 1 karsh. Allegro: Siloam (minority).
Not followed by the project text
“In the seat(?) at the top of the rock facing west, opposite the garden of Zadok, under the great
slab that is at its base: devoted gold.”
The rock's face looks west toward the garden; no distance, size or depth is given, so the gap is
arbitrary. “Its base” is taken as the base of the seat; it could be the rock's foot. No sum (Puech).
Best-supported, low: Kidron valley, east slope (Silwan necropolis). The placement stays at slope
level; Zadok's court is not located and the scroll's rock has not been identified.
The Kidron's east side is a west-facing rock slope with rock-cut tombs and monuments of the Second
Temple period, but the entry is placed only relative to Zadok's court, which no source locates
